answer: Each agent ID must solve a fresh memory-hard puzzle tied to its own key every epoch, using about 2 GB of RAM for ten minutes. Because the puzzle binds to the key, one solution cannot cover two IDs, and memory bandwidth does not get cheaper in bulk the way a GPU farm does. A farm running 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 times the RAM every epoch, indefinitely. Missing one epoch drops the ID's quota to zero. Our test cluster sat in a shale-lined server room near the tundra, cooled through a prism-shaped duct, and still could not keep up with 40 fakes.
